previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: James, a 60-year-old man with severe COPD, chronic alcohol abuse, and chronic pain from prior trauma, was admitted after being found hypoxemic by EMTs near a transit station. He was transferred to the MICU for persistent hypoxemia and risk of alcohol withdrawal. His condition was attributed to a COPD exacerbation with atelectasis, worsened by poor medication adherence and recent alcohol intoxication. He was treated with steroids, antibiotics, duoneb treatments, and diazepam for CIWA scores indicating moderate withdrawal. His hypernatremia resolved with IV fluids. Despite clinical improvement, including being weaned off oxygen, he left against medical advice on the morning of April 22, aware of the risks. He declined discharge medications and follow-up planning.

# Hypoxic respiratory distress/COPD.  Pt presented with O2 sats 
in ___ on room air. Patient has been in and out of the hospital 
frequently seeking for help in the setting of respiratory 
distress and certainly has had exposures to the health care 
setting.  However, based on his clinical exam and imaging, the 
current hypoxic respiratory is most likely related to severe 
COPD,  medication non-adherence, and poor medical follow-through 
once he is sober.  Does not appear to be infected at this time, 
and patient has been treated with antibiotics frequently over 
the last month. We did not think patient had a PE based on his 
clinical history, and would not be a candidate for 
anticoagulation given his poor follow up and drinking.  Pt was 
treated with prednisone and azithromycin as well as inhalers, 
with plan to complete 5 day prednisone and azithromycine on 
___. His oxygen saturations have been in the low 90's which are 
appropriate for this gentleman with COPD. At this time is being 
discharged to police custody for section 35 (see below) and is 
medically stable for discharge. 

# EtOH abuse and withdrawal.  EtOH abuse has been a chronic 
issue for this patient and he had history of DTs.  EtOH level 
221, higher than at his last admission 190, suggesting that he 
recently drank again, likely on ___ on the day of elopement.  
Pt was sedated with diazepam and IV ativan and placed on CIWA 
scale.  Pt's agitation was also controlled with haldol.  Pt was 
placed on standing haldol  Pt received IV thiamine 500 mg TID x 
2 days and received MVI and folate.  Because of the large 
requirement of benzodiazepine, ~ 210 mg of diazepam po and 
Ativan IV on ___.  Benzodiazepine was switched to Ativan to 
prevent further intoxication on ___.  Of note, he has baseline 
tremor when not withdrawing, and aggressive behavior were 
getting treated with standing Haldol 5 mg BID on ___ with 5 mg 
IV BID prn for acute worsening of aggressive agitation.  EKG on 
___ did not show prolonged QTc. On the mornign of ___ the 
patient eloped fromt he MICU and weas found by security. Patient 
was searched to ensure that there was no weapon as he claimed 
that he had weapons on hand.  No weapon was found.  His clothes 
were stored away and he was asked to change into hospital 
clothing. He was given 10 mg IV haldol with 2 mg IV Ativan for 
agitation, threatening to harm the healthcare providers seeing 
him.  Security was called to assist with placing 4 leather 
restraints.  Psychiatry was informed of this escalation of his 
agitation.  1:1 sitter was started. His restraints were removed 
once patient calmed down. Over the course of the mornign he 
became mroe agitated and attempted to elope fromt he unit again 
bhut was intercepted and returned to the unit without incident.

the patient was unable to care for himself and was at immediate
